Stan sighed and rifled through the cabinet, his tall, muscular body contorted down into an uncomfortable position to better see where he was looking. Packages and packages of freeze-dried foodstuffs were somewhat neatly arranged in racks, the plastic wrappers sometimes crinkling as he flicked them aside to read the labels. Most of them were marked plain, rations for mercenaries, militaries, and for the tucked-away compartments in escape pods on larger ships; predictably they lacked the flavor and texture of the more colorful wrappers. He paused, eyes focused on the bold, black text that seemed to be designed specifically to piss him off.

"What kind of dickhead..." he mumbled, but instead of finishing he grabbed a cluster and tossed them up on the counter above without looking, his other hand fumbling around in the boxes that obviously contained liquid as they sloshed around when disturbed.

Then he felt a familiar claw run up his t-shirt part way before the whole hand slipped under and ran gracefully over his many scars. He sighed and moved off to the side, his old knees and ankles creaking and cracking with muffled pops and familiar pain.

"What do you think? Milk?" he asked, cocking his head down to see if he was missing anything else in the dark.

Inzili pursed her lips as she thought, a brief moment passing. "For Jade? She is fat enough," she snickered, "get her healthy thing."

Though she didn't have malicious intent, Inzili would have never said that in front of Jade who had developed a habit of looking like a hurt puppy when her weight was brought up. Truthfully she didn't notice at first, but she was sure Stan had missed this and didn't quite know how to bring up the subject without stirring up trouble. She ran her claws up over his shoulder and smirked as she felt the powerful muscles of his shoulders work, his arm reaching deep before plucking out some sort of sweet juice. She looked at the label carefully when it was presented and plucked it from his hand, giving him a pat of approval.

"She really ain't fat, you know."

They had a dynamic between them that was missing between Stan and Jade, a rare accident of instinct and intuition of two different members of two very different species coming together in harmony. For her he was an obedient male, deep in her brain was a set of instructions to dominate her male mates and to take the role of leadership in a family unit. Stan's affectionate, understanding nature that came from his wholesome, but isolated, upbringing played right into this right up until he dissented.

Leaning down she whispered, "don't talk back," into his ear before nipping his neck.

"Don't y'all be gettin' frisky now, we ain't even had breakfast," Stan warned, but his grin betrayed him as he pulled himself up to stand. "Unless you wanna have a go on the counter again."

"Who is being frisky now?" she teased, humoring the proposal before remembering the burns she caught from their last attempt. "Behave."

That alluring grin he wore didn't subside, oh he *clearly* remembered what had happened, but he wisely didn't offer any further commentary. Patience was something she had in spades when the situation was right, and she waited just long enough for his guard to drop before swatting his crotch with a backhand.

"I say behave," she giggled, deftly avoiding an attempt to swat her backside. "Mmm, maybe I let you make it up to me, yes?"

Wincing he leaned against the counter and muttered, "I don't negotiate with terrorists."

"Do you still love me?"

Tearing open a package he considered his answer, quickly testing a few options in his mind as he leaned over and gave her a gentle peck on the cheek. "I'm going to face-fuck you so hard tonight."

"You *do* love me," she laughed, "to think I was worried for nothing!"

Clearly she was quite amused with herself, but she wondered if such antics could be normal for her kind. Often she compared this alien, human-oriented life she lived with the upbringing of her tribe, always measuring to see if she was normal. Was it normal to love? Did she love? Surely it wasn't normal to bring herself to his level (or to elevate him to her level, she didn't quite know) because that would not have been accepted in the strict matriarchal society she had come from. Maybe it wasn't normal, maybe *she* wasn't normal, and she huffed through her nostrils as that thought ate at her. Of course she wasn't normal, both her mates were aliens and one was of the race that oppressed her kind. She was worse than abnormal!

As if on cue her human lover caught the emotional spiral and twisted it somewhere else, his arms around her midsection was enough to soothe her. "Darlin' what's on your mind?"

"I think too much, is nothing."

Stan analyzed the statement, the word "bullshit" on the tip of his tongue ready to leap free. Instead he pressed his lips to the rough, purple scales of her neck and nodded in silent agreement. Sometimes it was best to leave her be.

"How you wanna cook this? Want me to do it?"

Cooking was male work, after all, and she stepped aside to admire him as he worked. Somehow he could take the bland "spacer food" that they had and make it palatable, she had watched him do it many times but couldn't replicate it. Within minutes the small oven pinged to indicate that it's task was done, but this was just a formality as the smell of the hot food had already heralded how ready it was. With an eager "mmm" Inzili took the hefty tray out and looked down at the breakfast meal, leaning over to plant a gentle kiss on Stan's cheek as he added the beverage boxes. He followed her as she carried the tray to their quarters, or what she probably subconsciously thought was their nest or something, a thought that brought out a chuckle.
